title: Work Tracking QA
eyebrow: QA · background work tracking (parent issue #396, "every layer of delegated work is one tap away"), house-rules 2.73.2

short.lead: Background work tracking is built on branch claude/project-thread-42w8p3 as house-rules 2.73.2. In a claude.ai project thread, four things now happen. The thread gets its own transcript link for its checklist header. A Remote Control session's link is asked for as soon as the session starts. Each finished helper's commands are written to a file in the shared project folder. If any of those links was never posted, the end of a turn is blocked once. verify.py passes all 951 checks and verify_tools.py all 47. Three of the four parts were also run against this thread's own real data, as the rows below say. Two things only you can test, because this session loaded an older version at start: a new project thread running 2.73.2, and a real Remote Control session.
short.hint: Tap a row to see what was checked and how.
items: Five new verify.py cases pass. I also ran the session-start hook with this thread's real environment: it produced the link to session_018ddrfbUqBBFUVGmxxEzptr, which is this thread's transcript, with the raw id cse_018ddrfbUqBBFUVGmxxEzptr beside it.

Five new verify.py cases pass: the hook fires on a started or already-running result, and stays silent on an asked result, outside a project thread, and with HOUSE_RULES_WORKTRACKING=off. It has not seen a real Remote Control start yet.

Four new verify.py cases pass. I also rendered the real transcript of the helper that built the thread link. The file in the project folder lists its 19 shell commands, from the first git status to the final commit. The first verify run wrote two test files into the real project folder, so the tests now default to a temporary folder, and a rerun left the project folder untouched.

Eight new verify.py cases pass. I also ran the check over this thread's real transcript. It flagged the checklists I posted before the thread link existed (4 of 9 lacked it). From the first checklist that carried the link onward, it said nothing.
Try it in a new project thread
After 2.73.2 is installed, start a new thread in a claude.ai project and ask it for any task that uses a helper agent, then one that starts a Remote Control session on your PC.

Check three things: the checklist header links to the thread's transcript, a helper's work-trail file is attached, and "Transcript of the session on your PC" is posted without you asking. Open each one.
